parts.text:
8
Explain the main principles behind the use of nuclear magnetic resonance imaging (NMRI) to
obtain diagnostic information about internal body structures.
[8]

markscheme_points.text: allows position of nuclei to be located
any two of the points marked (1)

hints: Hint 1: Explain the role of the strong uniform magnetic field in aligning the magnetic moments (spins) of hydrogen nuclei (protons) in the body.
Hint 2: Describe the two spin energy states produced by the magnetic field and the precession of protons at the Larmor frequency.
Hint 3: Explain the role of the radio-frequency (RF) pulse transmitted perpendicular to the main field at the Larmor frequency.
Hint 4: Describe how protons absorb RF energy through magnetic resonance and flip into the higher energy spin state.
Hint 5: Describe relaxation: what happens when the RF pulse stops and protons return to the lower energy equilibrium state.
Hint 6: Explain that during relaxation, the precessing protons emit RF signals that are detected by receiver coils.
Hint 7: Explain the purpose of a non-uniform magnetic field (gradient coils) superimposed on the uniform field.
Hint 8: Connect how the gradient field varies the Larmor frequency across the body, allowing precise spatial localization to form an image.
parts.proper_answer: strong uniform magnetic field radio-frequency pulse (applied) causes resonance/excitation (of nuclei)/nuclei absorb energy on relaxation/de-excitation, nuclei emit r.f./pulse non-uniform magnetic fiel
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
strong uniform magnetic field radio-frequency pulse (applied) causes resonance/excitation (of nuclei)/nuclei absorb energy on relaxation/de-excitation, nuclei emit r.f./pulse non-uniform magnetic fiel
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
